source: Wikipedia: Computational creativity (Boden's types)
finding: Boden splits creativity into exploratory, combinational and transformational. Transformational means deliberately transforming or transcending the space, by rejecting constraints that define the space or the problem. It is called more radical and rarer than exploratory.
numbers: Boden The Creative Mind 1990; Computer Models of Creativity 1999; P-creativity vs H-creativity distinction named.
limits: Encyclopedia summary, not the primary book. Page text read only to char 100000 of 124305.
agent_relevance: Gives the operator vocabulary: O4 (drop a constraint) and O8 (reframe) are the transformational moves; exploratory search is the default.

source: Wikipedia: Computational creativity (Wiggins formalisation)
finding: Wiggins formalised Boden's ideas in 'A Preliminary Framework for Description, Analysis and Comparison of Creative Systems' (Knowledge-Based Systems 19(7), 2006, pp 449-458).
numbers: Citation only. Page does not describe rules R, T, E or traversal.
limits: The CSF details themselves were NOT opened here (Wiggins 2006 PDF not retrieved; search budget gone). Second-hand descriptions in a05, a06, a27 only.
agent_relevance: Pointer to the formal base: transformation = change of the rules that define the space.

source: Espirito Santo, Wiggins, Cardoso (2024) Towards a Formal Creativity Theory: Preliminary results in Novelty and Transformativeness
finding: Recasts creativity with Formal Learning Theory (Gold 1967). A conceptual space is a class of recursively enumerable sets, a hypothesis is a program, the agent is a 'scientist' mapping data to hypotheses. Transformational creativity is a change of the agent's hypothesis caused by an artefact.
numbers: Definitions 1-7 (language, grammar, text, scientist, identification, artefact). Formalises novelty VN and transformativeness VTr of an artefact a in situation s=(agent, experience).
limits: Theory only, no experiments. Binary value only (valuable or not), like Wiggins rule E. Authors say multi-rule scientists (full CSF) is future work.
agent_relevance: Transformation is a change in the hypothesis space driven by new data, not by random novelty. Fits G2: revise from real failing output.

source: Espirito Santo, Wiggins, Cardoso (2024) Theorems 1-2
finding: Theorem 1: a novel artefact is not necessarily transformative. Theorem 2: a transformative artefact is not necessarily novel. So novelty is neither sufficient nor necessary for transformation in general.
numbers: Proved by constructing a simple scientist (confidence counter that flips hypothesis when confidence hits zero) for each case.
limits: Toy learners; the proofs show logical possibility, not frequency in real agents.
agent_relevance: Do not use 'is it novel?' as the test for a reframe. A reframe is good if it changes what the agent believes about the space and the check improves.

source: Espirito Santo, Wiggins, Cardoso (2024) Theorem 3
finding: If the learner is set-driven (ignores order of data, only the inspiring set matters), novelty IS necessary for transformativeness: an artefact already in the set cannot change the hypothesis.
numbers: Condition 1: content(s)=content(t) implies M(s)=M(t). Then Ia - I = {a}, so a is novel.
limits: Holds only for set-driven scientists. Order-sensitive learners (sequence of experiences) break it.
agent_relevance: An LLM context that is a bag of past attempts behaves set-driven: repeating a seen idea cannot shift it. Argues for novelty filters on proposed reframes (history of directions tried).

source: Schapiro, Black, Varshney (2025) Transformational Creativity in Science: A Graphical Theory
finding: Models a scientific conceptual space as a directed acyclic graph of constraints; sink nodes are axioms, other nodes are rules depending on axioms. Proves that edits to axioms have the largest transformative potential, because they invalidate all dependents.
numbers: Definition 1 DAG S=(V,E), V subsets of language L; prereq(v), depends(v). Case study: geocentric to heliocentric (Earth stationary + uniform circular motion becomes Sun central + elliptical orbits; Almagest, epicycles, 24-h day as dependents).
quote: Boden's insight that transformational creativity arises from changes in the enabling constraints
limits: Short paper. Illustrative historical fits, no empirical test, no LLM run. Graph is hand-built.
agent_relevance: Gives a computable rule for O4: rank constraints by number of dependents; drop the one with most dependents first for a big reframe, the one with fewest for a safe reframe.

source: Schapiro et al. (2025) background on Kuhn mapping
finding: Maps Boden onto Kuhn: normal science = exploratory or combinatorial puzzle solving; anomaly and crisis = loosening of rules; revolution = new constraint configuration. Cites Toivanen et al. 2018 (meta-level modules modify the constraints of the song search space) and Wiggins 2006 (transformation = exploratory search over the space of generative systems).
numbers: Phases I-III of Kuhn. Cites Wiggins 2006, Ritchie 2006, Toivanen 2018.
limits: Secondary description of Wiggins and Toivanen; originals not opened.
agent_relevance: Matches S-state logic: reframe only after an anomaly signal (impasse or failed check), as in G1.

source: Liapis, Martinez, Togelius, Yannakakis (2013/2021) Transforming Exploratory Creativity with DeLeNoX
finding: First working loop that alternates exploration and transformation. Exploration = feasible-infeasible novelty search over CPPN spaceship sprites. Transformation = a denoising autoencoder trained on the found set, then its encoding becomes the new distance function for the next exploration round.
numbers: 49x49 pixel sprites; 1000 spaceships per exploration phase; 64 features per transformation; diversity = mean Euclidean distance over all pairs in the training set; static run (features fixed from first set) compared with transforming run.
quote: Changing the distance function amounts to changing the exploration process of novelty search
limits: Diversity measured by the system's own learned metric; no human rating of creativity. No persistent archive across iterations, so simple shapes recur. One domain.
agent_relevance: Concrete recipe for O6 (change representation): after a search saturates, learn a new distance or feature space from what was found and search again in it. The history-of-directions log in S3 plays the archive role.

source: Liapis et al. DeLeNoX: transforming run vs static run
finding: In the transforming run, the highest diversity score for a feature set was usually reached on the training set of the next iteration; the static run's features lost power as exploration moved on. Transformation re-aligns search to visually diverse artefacts.
numbers: Figure 7 (diversity per iteration, scale about 3.2 to 4.6). Exact values only in figures.
limits: Numbers read from text, not from the plotted data. Claim is about the algorithm's own metric.
agent_relevance: Supports a rule: re-derive the diversity metric after each round, do not keep a fixed one.

source: Grachten, Chacon (2017) Strategies for Conceptual Change in Convolutional Neural Networks
finding: Treats transformational creativity as adaptation of a learned representation to a new task. Compares strategies on MNIST digits, natural images and classical music. Adaptive strategies beat learning from scratch in training effort and under scarce data.
numbers: Classification target: keep first-layer convolutional filters, reset the rest, works best (even from an autoencoder source). Autoencoding target: reuse the full model works from the start but then stops improving.
quote: Adaptive strategies are systematically more effective than a baseline method that starts learning from scratch
limits: Report from the Lrn2Cre8 project; authors say no single strategy wins and longer training is needed. No clear advantage of prior regularisation. This is transfer learning relabelled as creativity; no creative-output judging.
agent_relevance: Weak analogue only: when stuck, keep low-level parts (facts, objects) and reset higher-level framing. Not a measured prompt result.

source: Suzuki, Banaei-Kashani (2025/2026) Universe of Thoughts (T-UoT)
finding: Implements Boden's transformational mode as an LLM procedure: extract rules, generate k=5 rule transformations, score each with 3 binary flags (goal preserved, difficulty preserved, solution space opened), keep passing ones, select, reframe the problem, then run creative search.
numbers: Algorithm: LLMpropose(EXTRACTRULES), LLMpropose(GENERATETRANSFORMATIONS, |R|=k=5), LLMscore b_goal,b_diff,b_space in {0,1}, REFRAME(P,R), CREATIVESEARCH.
limits: Selection and scoring are done by the LLM itself (G4/G6 concern). Immutable constraints H are supplied by the task.
agent_relevance: Ready-made template for O4 plus O8 with a goal-preserved check. The b_goal flag blocks a reframe that changes the answer being asked for.

source: Suzuki, Banaei-Kashani Table 1: three new creative-reasoning tasks (GPT-4o)
finding: T-UoT scored highest among matched GPT-4o methods on Bridge and Electricity, but not Society. Human-rated creativity (mean of novelty and utility).
numbers: Bridge human: T-UoT 0.680 vs OnePrompt 0.480, CoT 0.590, ToT 0.580, EGoT 0.650. Electricity human: T-UoT 0.620 vs OnePrompt 0.540, CoT 0.560. Society human: T-UoT 0.550 vs CoT 0.500, ToT 0.530, EGoT 0.560, C-UoT 0.560. 10 generations per method and task; human-LLM score correlation r=0.708.
limits: Tiny sample (10 generations per cell, 3 tasks). Differences are 0.03 to 0.2 on a 0-1 scale with no confidence intervals. On Society T-UoT does not win; DeepSeek V3.1 reaches 0.720 human score.
agent_relevance: Reframing helps on low-constraint, clearly specified tasks only. Do not make O4/O8 a default; fire on a signal (G1).

source: Suzuki, Banaei-Kashani Table 2: HypoArena, Qwen3-14B (100 tasks)
finding: On the independent hypothesis benchmark (34 bio, 34 ML, 32 social tasks) T-UoT ranks 6th of 7, above only plain OnePrompt. Exploratory UoT is best.
limits: Judge is a small LLM; two other judges keep the E-UoT advantage (agreement 0.59-0.79) with 2.6-5.4% hard reversals. With GLM-4-9B, OnePrompt ranks first, so the ordering depends on backbone.
agent_relevance: In constrained tasks transformation did NOT beat plain search. Transformation is not a free upgrade; keep exploratory search as default.

source: Suzuki, Banaei-Kashani ablation and cost
finding: Removing rule transformation from T-UoT costs only a small preference. T-UoT is also the most expensive method.
numbers: Ablation, full vs ablated pairwise win (chance 50%): T-UoT 54.2% (bio 54.1, ML 53.4, social 55.1); C-UoT 58.3%; E-UoT 52.4%. Tokens per task on 10-task audit: OnePrompt 3.7k, CoT 3.5k, ToT 27.1k, E-UoT 36.7k, C-UoT 134.3k, T-UoT 193.3k (52.5x OnePrompt).
limits: Cost audit on 10 tasks only. Failure trace: T-UoT may fail to propagate consequences of the chosen rule change.
agent_relevance: About 52x token cost for a 4 point edge over ablation. Use O4/O8 sparingly and cap budget.

source: Sun et al. (2025) OMEGA: Can LLMs Reason Outside the Box in Math?
finding: Benchmark built on Boden's typology: exploratory (harder instance in same frame), compositional, transformative (the familiar tactic fails or is intractable; a new tactic such as symmetry substitution is needed). Programmatic templates with verified answers across six domains.
numbers: Transformative set: seven categories. Example: x^5+10x^3+20x-4 needs a symmetry substitution, not the rational-root tactic.
limits: Template-based maths only. 'Transformative' here means new tactic, not new value system.
agent_relevance: Direct test of 'drop the failing tactic'. It is verifiable, so usable as our own G3 check bench.

source: OMEGA RL results on transformative generalization (Qwen)
finding: RL on the familiar tactic did not teach the new one. Base accuracy typically below 20% on transformative OOD items; after RL OOD stays low, often 0%.
numbers: Only notable OOD gain: Setting 7, +10 pp, and trajectories showed naive solutions on easy variants. In-domain gain e.g. +56% on matrix rank. Matrix rank OOD: base 70%, after RL fell 30 pp. Exploratory contrast: Zebra Logic base 30%, RL +61 ID, +53 OOD. Compositional: mostly about +6%, GCD plus polynomial roots no gain.
quote: Transformational capabilities may require explicit exposure to diverse problem-solving strategies
limits: Fine-tuning study on Qwen-series, not prompting. Does not say a scaffold cannot help.
agent_relevance: Training on outcome reward can entrench the old tactic. A scaffold that forces a named alternative tactic is the cheap thing to test.

source: Sun et al. OMEGA frontier models
finding: Frontier reasoning models degrade sharply as problem complexity grows; in the transformative setting all models struggle with special-function intersections and some polynomial problems. CoT traces show early solution then long over-verification.
numbers: Models: DeepSeek-R1, o3-mini, o4-mini, Claude 3.7 Sonnet. OpenAI models best on compositional matrix rank and polynomials.
limits: Per-model transformative numbers only in figures.
agent_relevance: Overthinking after the answer is found supports counted stops over free self-checking.

source: Qian et al. (2025) EscapeBench: Towards Advancing Creative Intelligence of Language Model Agents
finding: Room-escape games need unconventional tool use and implicit goals. Models with working memory and CoT reach only about 15% average progress without hints. Best models need up to ten times optimal steps.
numbers: GPT-4o BaseAgent: 7.17 hints, 593.92 steps, 48.89% early-exit progress; small models (Qwen2.5-7B etc.) need ~1500 steps. 36 games; each needs at least 100 steps and 40 bottleneck actions.
quote: Current agents still significantly lack creativity in novel tool use
limits: Hints given after 50 idle steps shape the metric. Game text may be in training data.
agent_relevance: A creative leap from affordance (hard stick as lever) is the failure; supports an O6 prompt that lists object properties without the usual use.

source: EscapeAgent: Foresight and Reflection modules
finding: A scaffold with Foresight (propose and check tool-use hypotheses before acting) and Reflection (keep an unsolved-task list) cut hints and steps without any training.
numbers: GPT-4o: BaseAgent 7.17 hints 593.9 steps -> EscapeAgent 5.00 hints 452.0 steps (Reflection only 6.75/570; Foresight only 9.83/707). Llama-3.1-70B: 14.67/981 -> 7.17/625. Reported up to 40% fewer steps and hints.
limits: Same benchmark for design and test. Single run averages. Ablation order inconsistent across models.
agent_relevance: The only scaffold in this set with a measured gain on creative moves. Both pieces are code-trackable (task list), matching our program-decides rule.

source: Franceschelli, Musolesi (2023/2025) On the Creativity of Large Language Models
finding: Argues LLMs can give value and a weak novelty and surprise, but transformational creativity is not achievable with current training: RLHF or DPO alignment narrows diversity and training stays probabilistic. They suggest different architectures or fine-tuning that lets the model forget learned rules.
numbers: Conceptual analysis; no experiments. Cites Kirk et al. 2024 (alignment lowers diversity).
quote: Transformational creativity is not achievable through the current LLM training solutions.
limits: Opinion/philosophy, no measurement. A 2023 argument; later scaffolds like T-UoT were not considered.
agent_relevance: Warns that sampling plus alignment make rule-breaking rare. Our scaffold should supply the rule change from outside the model (code picks which constraint to drop).

source: Magrin-Chagnolleau (2026) Can an AI System Be Creative?
finding: Uses Boden to argue AI is capable in combinatorial creativity, bounded in exploratory, and fundamentally incapable of transformational creativity; missing piece is chance and serendipity and a subject to recognise it.
numbers: Position paper; proposes human-AI collaboration, concrete experiments described but not statistically tested here. Notes Boden died July 2025.
limits: Strong claim without measurement; contradicted in part by T-UoT and EscapeAgent results above on narrow tasks.
agent_relevance: Counter-view to log: the human may be the part that recognises a good rule change. Keep as a user-in-loop option.

source: Schapiro et al. (2025/2026) KOMBINE: Measuring Combinatorial Creativity in LLMs and Humans
finding: 35 LLMs and 75 humans on combinatorial creativity. Transformational creativity is described but not tested in this paper.
numbers: LLMs 10-16 points better at association and analogy than at blends; one in five invented concepts reuses another model's properties; same-provider models 2.3x more likely to reuse; humans score below nearly every LLM.
limits: Combinatorial only; it defers transformational creativity to TwistBench (plot twists, Schapiro et al. 2026b, not opened).
agent_relevance: Shows model homogeneity (G4): samples from related models share inventions, so more samples will not give a different space.

source: Schapiro et al. (2026) Assessing the Creativity of LLMs: Testing, Limits, and New Frontiers
finding: Human creativity tests (DAT, RAT) have unproven validity for LLMs; no existing test reliably predicts scientific ideation. Authors name transformational creativity as understudied and point to OMEGA and EscapeBench as the early empirical tests.
numbers: Introduces DRAT, only significant predictor of scientific ideation. DAT best for creative writing; Conditional DAT best for divergent thinking.
limits: Automated tests only; no transformational test run.
agent_relevance: Do not use DAT-like scores as proof of a reframe working (G3: need held-out check).

source: Marco, Gonzalo, Mateo (2024) Pron vs Prompt: GPT-4 vs a top novelist
finding: Boden-inspired rubric used by literary experts on 30 titles from each side (60 stories). GPT-4 is far from the top novelist; GPT-4 wrote more creatively from the author's titles than from its own, and better in English than Spanish.
numbers: 5,400 manual assessments per search summary; abstract and intro read, results tables not read.
limits: Rubric covers value/novelty/surprise, not transformation specifically. One author, one model era.
agent_relevance: Evidence that a human-seeded direction beats the model's own choice: choose the direction by code or user, not by the model.

source: Nagarajan, Wu, Ding, Raghunathan (2025) Roll the dice and look before you leap
finding: Minimal algorithmic tasks for combinational and exploratory creativity. Next-token learning is myopic; teacherless and diffusion models give more diverse, original output. Noise at the input (seed-conditioning) matches or beats output temperature.
numbers: Seed-conditioning gives diverse output even with greedy decoding; improvement strongest on exploratory tasks.
limits: Tests combinational and exploratory creativity only, small models trained from scratch, not the transformational type.
agent_relevance: Randomness in the prompt (random seed word, random constraint) can replace temperature when forcing different directions.

source: Aggregate: what the open literature lacks
finding: As of mid-2026 the only measured LLM tests tied to transformational creativity found in this search are OMEGA, EscapeBench and the UoT paper. Others are theory papers. No replication of any of them found.
numbers: Search covered arXiv (partly rate limited), one web search, OpenAlex (budget exhausted), Semantic Scholar (empty).
limits: Absence of evidence here reflects limited search, not proof. TwistBench, Spark and Wiggins 2006 not opened.
agent_relevance: Keep O4/O6/O8 at [S]. Plan an own test: drop-constraint variant on a verifiable bench vs plain.

source: Toivanen et al. (2018) via Schapiro 2025
finding: Described as an architecture for transformational creativity in generative systems where meta-level modules change the constraints governing the song search space.
numbers: No numbers seen.
limits: Second-hand only; the original was not opened.
agent_relevance: Same pattern as DeLeNoX: a meta layer changes the space, the base layer searches.

source: Wiggins (2006) Creative Systems Framework via Santo 2024 and Liapis
finding: As described by opened papers: CSF defines a rule set R for the conceptual space, a traversal strategy T and an evaluation E; transformation is search at the meta level over these. Santo et al. note CSF value rules are binary.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Second-hand. CSF primary text not retrieved.
agent_relevance: Gives three levers for the agent to vary: constraints (R), search strategy (T), evaluation criterion (E).
